      Guccimillk
      2 stars out of 5
      Rated 10/25/2026
      MW4 Standard
      DMZ: A PvE Mission Game Disguised as an Extraction Shooter

      DMZ feels like a PvE mission game with extraction bolted onto it, rather than a PvPvE sandbox where other players make every deployment unpredictable. I wanted to like the new DMZ, but I find it boring, disconnected, and lacking the tension that should define an extraction shooter. My biggest complaint is the lack of meaningful PvP. Matches feel overwhelmingly PvE, with long stretches of fighting endless AI, looting, and completing repetitive objectives without encountering other players. The lack of consistent, unpredictable operator encounters leaves the experience feeling empty and removes much of the excitement that makes extraction games compelling. The game is also overly punishing when you fail to extract. Losing gear is part of the genre, but charging increasingly expensive fees to revive higher-level operators adds another penalty on top of losing your equipment and loot. This feels less like meaningful risk and more like a punishment that discourages experimentation and continued play. The looting system feels completely disconnected from the setting. Why am I stopping in the middle of a war zone to search a refrigerator for plastic parts? It makes no sense in the context of a military operation. Instead of immersion, I'm left doing arbitrary scavenging tasks that feel designed to extend playtime rather than enhance the experience. Missions quickly become repetitive, while AI enemies are more frustrating than challenging, seemingly to spawn endlessly from behind you and overwhelming you through sheer numbers. Progression is equally underwhelming. The skill tree offers minor percentage improvements to already existing skills rather than meaningful changes to gameplay. The FOB is clunky and unintuitive, forcing you to run between different stations just to manage your loadout and upgrades. The map also lacks the atmosphere and environmental storytelling needed to make exploration worthwhile. To sum up my frustrations, the endless empty grind, cumbersome menus, endless AI, and lack of meaningful operator encounters ultimately, left me feeling like DMZ is a collection of systems rather than a cohesive, living military sandbox. More crafting, materials, and missions don't automatically create depth. I want meaningful progression, believable encounters, and the constant uncertainty of running into other players. Right now, this feels like a PvE looting simulator with extraction mechanics, not the tense, unpredictable DMZ experience I was hoping for.

      Call of Duty®: Modern Warfare® 4

      Share your thoughts and help other players in the community.

      War erupts on the Korean Peninsula as North Korea launches a full-scale invasion that threatens to destabilize the world in Call of Duty®: Modern Warfare® 4.

      A young squad of South Korean soldiers fight to survive on the collapsing front lines, while half a world away a vengeful Captain Price wages a personal war from the shadows as he stays one step ahead of those hunting him. As Price’s off-book mission collides with the forces behind the invasion, the war spreads beyond anyone’s control.

      Modern Warfare® 4 pushes the series into darker and more dangerous territory, where consequence and escalation bring long-running storylines to a powerful and emotional breaking point.

      - Campaign drops players into trench warfare in Korea, close-quarters combat in New York, high-octane chases through Paris, SAS night raids in Mumbai, and city-wide assaults to reclaim occupied territory.
      - Multiplayer delivers grounded, precise combat where fluid movement, player choice, and greater control define every engagement.
      - In DMZ, players operate as an off-the-books asset behind enemy lines, where every extraction run into contested territory forces hard choices about which objectives to pursue, what to secure, and when to get out.
